title: The Coen Brothers
subtitle: eighteen together, five apart
blurb: The eighteen features Joel and Ethan made together, plus the five solo films with a note saying whose — about 38 hours.
notes: Credits were odd for twenty years.

Until The Ladykillers, Joel alone took the directing credit and Ethan the producing credit, and they edited under the shared pseudonym Roderick Jaynes. The filmography credits them jointly on all eighteen; so does this list.
Their segments of the anthology films Paris, je t'aime and Chacun son cinéma, The Naked Man (Ethan co-wrote it, nobody named Coen directed it), and the scripts and producing jobs for other directors.
From Wikidata, in hours, for the 22 films that are out.
Filmography from Wikipedia's Coen brothers filmography; runtimes from Wikidata.

sections.title: The independents
sections.intro: Blood Simple through The Big Lebowski: seven films of murders misfiring and kidnappings going wrong, with Fargo the point where the Academy caught up. Ethan went uncredited as co-director until 2004 — they were always both directing.

sections.title: The studio decade
sections.intro: O Brother through A Serious Man — three George Clooney pictures, a black-and-white noir, a Ladykillers remake, and No Country for Old Men, which won them Best Picture, Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay at once.

sections.title: Late together
sections.intro: A western from the Portis novel, a folk singer going nowhere, old Hollywood, and an anthology western — the last film they made as a pair.

sections.title: Solo
sections.intro: After Buster Scruggs they worked apart for a stretch — Joel toward Shakespeare, Ethan toward a Jerry Lee Lewis documentary and two lesbian B-movie capers. Each row says whose film it is.
